title_en: Hong Kong Mei Yi Metal Products Factory v. China Patent Office Patent Reexamination Board — appeal dispute over confirmation of invention patent right for "Inertia Clamp Door"
keywords_en: administrative; administrative dispute over patent invalidation declaration; second instance; High People's Court; Beijing Municipality; legal person; state organ; Patent Law; determination of inventiveness; determination of technical field; combination of prior art documents; reversal; invention patent; invalidation declaration; examination of inventiveness; patent right; dispute over invention patent right
full_text_en:
Hong Kong Mei Yi Metal Products Factory v. Patent Reexamination Board of the China Patent Office — appeal case concerning confirmation of invention patent right for "inertia clamp-type door"

Appellant (original defendant): Patent Reexamination Board of the China Patent Office.

Legal Representative: Zhao Yuanguo, Deputy Director.

Agent ad litem: Yin Xintian, Reexamination Commissioner of the Patent Reexamination Board of the China Patent Office.

Agent ad litem: Zhang Shuhua, Reexamination Commissioner of the Patent Reexamination Board of the China Patent Office.

Appellee (original plaintiff): Hong Kong Mei Yi (Zhu Ji) Metal Products Factory.

Legal Representative: Chen Fuyou, Director.

Agent ad litem: Lou Chuipin, lawyer of China Global Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Song Min, patent agent of China Patent Agent (Hong Kong) Ltd.

The appellant, Patent Reexamination Board of the China Patent Office (hereinafter referred to as the Patent Reexamination Board), dissatisfied with the administrative judgment of the Beijing Intermediate People's Court in the case concerning dispute over confirmation of invention patent right for "inertia clamp-type door," filed an appeal to the Beijing High People's Court. The court found upon trial the following:

On April 1, 1985, Hong Kong Mei Yi (Zhu Ji) Metal Products Factory (hereinafter referred to as Hong Kong Mei Yi Factory) filed an application with the China Patent Office for an invention patent titled "inertia clamp-type door." After substantive examination, the China Patent Office considered that the invention satisfied the requirements of novelty, inventiveness, and practical applicability under the Chinese Patent Law, and granted the patent right on June 23, 1988, under Patent No. 85101517. After examination and approval by the China Patent Office, the invention patent had fourteen claims. The main technical composition disclosed in its independent claim was: an inertia clamp-type door, wherein the diagonal bars of the door lattice are connected to the vertical straight bars of the door posts, the diagonal bars rotate and are fixed at a fixed position on a first intermediate vertical straight bar, and are rotatably and slidably connected to a second vertical straight bar; at least the second vertical straight bar has a channel-shaped cross-section and has a recessed flange on its side walls; the means for connecting the diagonal bars to the second vertical straight bar includes a pin shaft that passes through the diagonal bars, characterized in that at the ends of the pin shaft, bushings with an H-shaped cross-section in the transverse direction of the shaft are installed, and the flange of the vertical straight bar is installed in the groove of the H-shaped cross-section bushing. The object of the invention was to provide a device for connecting the diagonal bars and the vertical straight bars of the inertia clamp-type door that is not only simple in structure but also improves the rigidity of the door, making the opening and closing movement light and quiet.

Between May 1989 and March 1990, the Panyu County La Zha Factory, Hongxing Juan Zha Factory, and Nanfang La Zha Factory of Guangzhou City, Guangdong Province, respectively filed requests for invalidation with the Patent Reexamination Board on the grounds that the "inertia clamp-type door" invention patent lacked novelty and inventiveness. After examination, the Patent Reexamination Board, on the ground that the invention lacked inventiveness, made Examination Decision No. 112 on Invalidation Request on December 31, 1990, declaring the invention patent right of Patent No. 85101517 invalid. The prior art used as comparative documents in the examination by the Patent Reexamination Board was: UK Patent No. GB1361763 (hereinafter referred to as Comparative Document 1) and Japanese Patent Application Laid-Open No. Sho 59-14156 (hereinafter referred to as Comparative Document 2).

The main technical composition of Comparative Document 1 was: a folding gate having a plurality of vertically placed posts connected by crossbars, each of the plurality of posts having three channel-shaped members of the same cross-sectional shape; each post has a first channel-shaped member with louver hinges; a second channel-shaped member whose web is fixed to the web of the first channel-shaped member such that the open sides of the first and second channel-shaped members face away from each other; a third channel-shaped member having means for fixing the third channel-shaped member parallel to the first and second channel-shaped members with a spacing; the open sides of the second and third channel-shaped members face each other; the fixing means is the pivot of the crossbar member, extending between the second and third channel-shaped members through the open sides. The object of the invention in Comparative Document 1 was to reduce the number of different elements of the folding gate, i.e., to make the vertical straight bars universal, while avoiding the use of heavy manual riveting processes in assembling the gate.

The main technical composition of Comparative Document 2 was: a middle wheel device for a telescopic sliding gate, characterized in that C-shaped rods are symmetrically erected inwardly on both sides of the wheel frame of the middle wheel device, which are fixed to the outer sides of the symmetrical posts of the telescopic sliding gate; the upper sliding shaft and the lower fixed shaft supporting the symmetrical diagonal bars can be inserted into rectangular holes and circular holes provided on the symmetrical posts, and protrude outward from the symmetrical posts; a freely sliding sliding sleeve is mounted on the opening flange of the C-shaped rod; below the sliding sleeves at both ends of the sliding shaft on the C-shaped rod, a locking device capable of sliding freely up and down is provided. The object of the invention in Comparative Document 2 was to solve the problem of middle support for a garden telescopic sliding gate, reduce the load on the gate, make the opening and closing movement of the sliding gate light and smooth, and extend the service life of the wheels of the gate.

After examination, the Patent Reexamination Board found that Comparative Document 1, Comparative Document 2, and other comparative documents submitted by the requesters did not disclose all the technical features of the independent claim of the invention. Therefore, the "inertia clamp-type door" invention patent was novel. However, it lacked inventiveness. The reasons were: Comparative Document 1 was the closest prior art for assessing the inventiveness of the invention because it disclosed all the technical features of the independent claim except for the H-shaped bushing. Comparative Document 2 also disclosed a telescopic sliding gate. In that sliding gate, one end of the diagonal bar was pivotally connected to a fixed pin shaft, and the other end was pivotally connected to a sliding pin shaft, while at both ends of the pin shaft, sliding sleeves with an H-shaped cross-section were installed. When the gate was pulled, causing the inclination of the diagonal bars to change, the diagonal bars would drive the sliding pin shaft, through the sliding sleeves at its two ends, to slide freely up and down on the flange of the C-shaped cross-section rod. Clearly, the sliding sleeve was identical to the H-shaped cross-section bushing used in the invention in terms of its structure, its cooperation with other components, its functional principle, and the effects produced. Since Comparative Document 2 belonged to the same technical field as the invention and provided a usable technical solution to the technical problem that the invention aimed to solve, when comparing the "inertia clamp-type door" invention patent with Comparative Document 1 and Comparative Document 2, the content of the independent claim of the invention no longer possessed the prominent substantive feature as required by Article 22(3) of the Patent Law. Accordingly, Examination Decision No. 112 on Invalidation Request was made, declaring the invention patent right of Patent No. 85101517 for "inertia clamp-type door" invalid.

Hong Kong Mei Yi Factory, dissatisfied with the invalidation request examination decision of the Patent Reexamination Board, filed a lawsuit with the Beijing Intermediate People's Court within the statutory period. The main reasons were: Compared with the prior art existing before the filing date, the "inertia clamp-type door" invention had prominent substantive features and represented significant progress. Since the object of Comparative Document 2 was different from that of the invention, the technical fields were different, and that comparative document could not provide useful technical teaching for the technical problem to be solved by the invention, it was inappropriate for the Patent Reexamination Board to combine Comparative Document 2 with Comparative Document 1 to deny the inventiveness of the "inertia clamp-type door" invention. In assessing whether an invention was inventive, not only its technical solution but also its object and effects should be considered. The object of the "inertia clamp-type door" invention was to start from the overall rigidity of the inertia clamp-type door and solve the problems of high resistance, noise, and wear during opening and closing. To achieve the above invention object, the technical solution adopted by the invention was to install H-shaped cross-section bushings at both ends of the pin shaft connecting the end of each lattice diagonal bar to each vertical straight bar of the door. Due to the adoption of the above technical solution with substantive features, the invention achieved technical effects such as improving the overall rigidity of the door, making the door movement more stable, and reducing noise. It can be seen that compared with Comparative Document 1 and Comparative Document 2, the invention differed not only in its invention object and technical solution but also in the technical effects achieved. Therefore, if the object, technical solution, and effects of the invention were considered as a whole, it obviously had prominent substantive features. Even if Comparative Document 1 and Comparative Document 2 were combined and compared with the invention, the invention still possessed prominent substantive features and thus was inventive. The factory requested the court to revoke the invalidation decision of the Patent Reexamination Board and maintain the invention patent right of No. 85101517 effective.

The Patent Reexamination Board made a defense: Comparative Document 2 disclosed a sliding gate for garden use, with wheel frames for support at its middle and movable ends, whose function was similar to the ball devices installed at the bottom of some vertical straight bars shown in the drawings of the invention, except that the wheel frames were not confined to movement on a single bottom rail. In that sliding gate, the diagonal bars were connected to pin shafts, and the pin shafts, through sliding sleeves at their two ends, slid on the opening flanges of opposing C-shaped rods; the sliding sleeves installed at both ends of the sliding pin shaft and the fixed pin shaft had an H-shaped cross-section, and their concave portions could fit over the opening flanges of the C-shaped rods and could slide freely up and down. Clearly, this sliding mechanism was consistent with the corresponding mechanism in the invention in structure and movement mode; at the same time, it could also objectively achieve the effect of compact component assembly, smooth movement, and noise reduction, and thus was consistent with the effect of the corresponding mechanism in the invention. This was the reason why the Patent Reexamination Board, in its invalidation decision, considered that Comparative Document 2 provided useful technical teaching for solving the technical problem to be solved by the invention. Under such circumstances, the number of H-shaped bushings used could not constitute a substantive technical feature. The significance of Comparative Document 2 was that it provided teaching for installing H-shaped bushings at the sliding connection between the pin shaft and the channel-shaped vertical straight bar of the sliding gate. Once such technical teaching was known, applying it to other parts with the same structure would not require a person of ordinary skill in the art to make inventive mental efforts. Therefore, emphasizing the number of H-shaped components used did not help establish the inventiveness of the invention. Since a person of ordinary skill in the art could, without any inventive effort, use the relevant technical teaching of Comparative Document 2 to achieve the object of the invention, it was appropriate to combine the two comparative documents when assessing inventiveness. The overall invention object of Comparative Document 2 was different from that of the invention, and therefore Comparative Document 2 adopted some other mechanisms not included in the invention. However, as regards the objective purpose and effect of using the sliding sleeve component, it was consistent with the H-shaped bushing adopted in the invention. The mere fact that the invention object stated in a comparative document was different should not lead to the conclusion that the document was unsuitable for assessing the inventiveness of an invention, especially when the comparative document belonged to the same technical field as the invention and provided useful technical teaching for achieving the invention object of the invention. This was particularly true. Therefore, the Board requested the court to uphold the original invalidation decision.

The court of first instance held that: According to the provisions of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China, so-called inventiveness means that, compared with the prior art existing before the filing date, the invention has prominent substantive features and represents significant progress. In determining whether an invention is inventive, the invention object, technical solution, and technical effects of the invention should be considered as a whole. Although Comparative Document 1 disclosed the technical features of the preamble of the independent claim of the "inertia clamp-type door" invention, it did not possess the distinguishing technical features of the characterizing part of the invention. Therefore, there was a clear difference between Comparative Document 1 and Hong Kong Mei Yi Factory's invention. Although Comparative Document 2 disclosed a sliding sleeve with an H-shaped cross-section, whose concave portion could fit over the opening flange of the C-shaped rod and could slide freely up and down, that sliding sleeve was one of many technical features of the middle wheel device of the telescopic sliding gate, and its purpose was to cooperate with the locking device to solve the ground-bearing problem of the middle wheel of the garden fence gate. In contrast, the invention started from improving the overall rigidity of the door and reducing noise, and extensively adopted pin shafts with H-shaped bushings among the various vertical straight bars. Since the bushing was emphasized to be cylindrical, made of plastic or nylon, and a gasket was installed between the bushing and the diagonal bar, this not only avoided friction between metal parts but also caused the bushing and the flange, and the diagonal bars and the diagonal bars, to be compressed, thereby increasing the rigidity of the door, reducing noise, and making the movement light and effortless. It can be seen that the invention combined various technical means to make the bushing play more functions in the "inertia clamp-type door." Therefore, although Comparative Document 1 and Comparative Document 2 belonged to the same technical field as the invention, a person of ordinary skill in the art could not, starting from Comparative Document 1 and combining it with Comparative Document 2, directly obtain useful technical teaching about the invention. There were clear substantive differences between the invention and the comparative documents in terms of the invention object, the technical solution proposed to achieve that object, and the final technical effects. The invention was not obvious to a person of ordinary skill in the art combining the two comparative documents. Based on this, it was determined that Hong Kong Mei Yi Factory's Patent No. 85101517 "inertia clamp-type door" invention patent had prominent substantive features and complied with the provisions of the Chinese Patent Law regarding inventiveness. The reasons relied upon by the Patent Reexamination Board's Examination Decision No. 112 on Invalidation Request lacked sufficient evidence. In accordance with Article 22(3) of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 54(2) of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, it was adjudicated to revoke the Patent Reexamination Board's Examination Decision No. 112 on Invalidation Request.

The defendant, the Patent Reexamination Board, dissatisfied with the judgment, filed an appeal. The main reasons were: 1. The judgment applied the law improperly regarding the determination of inventiveness. On the one hand, when determining the technical content of the two cited comparative documents, it only took the claims in the comparative documents as prior art, without comprehensively identifying and analyzing the technical content recorded in the entire specification and drawings; on the other hand, when analyzing and determining the technical features of the invention patent, it deviated from the scope of protection claimed in the claims. For example, the judgment stated that "the material of the bushing is plastic or nylon" and "a gasket is installed between the bushing and the diagonal bar," but these features were not reflected in the claims of the invention patent. The judgment repeatedly emphasized that the invention object of Comparative Document 2 was different from that of the invention, and this determination constituted an important part of its reasoning. If the determination principle expressed in the judgment were adopted, it would not only seriously violate the provisions of the Chinese Patent Law but also be contrary to common practice worldwide. 2. The judgment had errors in determining facts. For instance, it wrote "Comparative Document 1 disclosed all technical features of claim 1 except the H-shaped bushing" as stated in the reasons of the invalidation decision as "Comparative Document 1 almost covered the preamble part of the independent claim of Hong Kong Mei Yi Factory's invention," whereas the invalidation decision never used the vague wording "almost covered"; for example, it determined that the "purpose" of using the H-shaped cross-section sliding sleeve in Comparative Document 2 "was to cooperate with the locking device to solve the ground-bearing problem of the middle wheel"; and for example, without specific analysis, the judgment enumerated several differences between the invention and Comparative Document 2 in terms of "the arrangement of lattice diagonal bars and vertical straight bars," etc., which were inconsistent with the facts. Therefore, the Board requested the appellate court to amend the judgment of the court of first instance regarding the improper application of law and errors in determining facts in assessing inventiveness, as well as its conclusion.

The appellee, Hong Kong Mei Yi Factory, in its defense, agreed with the conclusion of the judgment of the court of first instance, holding that the judgment appropriately applied the law regarding the determination of inventiveness, the determination principle was correct, and it also conformed to the practice of patent examination in China and abroad. It further emphasized that the technical solution of the invention had prominent substantive features compared with the prior art; the distinguishing technical feature in the independent claim of the invention (i.e., the H-shaped bushing) differed from the H-shaped cross-section sliding sleeve in Comparative Document 2 in purpose, mode, and function. It requested the appellate court to uphold the judgment of the court of first instance. At the same time, it considered that the judgment of the court of first instance had some inappropriate expressions in the wording of certain facts.

The Beijing High People's Court held that: According to Article 22(3) of the Patent Law, inventiveness means that, compared with the prior art existing before the filing date, the invention has prominent substantive features and represents significant progress. The so-called "prominent substantive features" means that, from the perspective of the historical development of the technical field, the invention, compared with the prior art, has a breakthrough in substantive technical content, causing a prominent substantive change in the field. The so-called "significant progress" means that the invention, compared with the closest existing prior art, has made substantial progress, which is usually manifested in overcoming the deficiencies and shortcomings of the prior art or having obvious technical effects. In this case, compared with the prior art, the invention had prominent substantive features and significant progress. The reasons are:

First, the independent claim of the "inertia clamp-type door" invention patent includes a preamble part and a characterizing part. Comparing the technical solution of the invention with the prior art, Comparative Document 1 disclosed all the technical features of the preamble part of the independent claim of the invention patent, while Comparative Document 2 did not further disclose the distinguishing technical features of the characterizing part of the independent claim of the invention patent. The characterizing part of the independent claim of the "inertia clamp-type door" invention patent was: "at the ends of the pin shaft, bushings with an H-shaped cross-section in the transverse direction of the shaft are installed, and the flange of the vertical straight bar is installed in the groove of the H-shaped cross-section bushing." This was the most essential technical feature of the mutual combination relationship among the main components in the overall structure of the invention patent. It was this H-shaped bushing and the combination relationship between the H-shaped bushing and the various vertical straight bars that made the invention have prominent substantive features. In contrast, Comparative Document 2 disclosed a middle wheel device for a telescopic sliding gate. The sliding gate involved therein was a gate with a completely different structure from the "inertia clamp-type door" of the invention. Although the wheel device in Comparative Document 2 also adopted an H-shaped cross-section sliding sleeve, this H-shaped cross-section sliding sleeve was only installed at the connection part between a pair of pin shafts and a pair of C-shaped rods on the middle wheel frame, sliding freely up and down, and could cooperate with a locking device on the C-shaped rods to enable the middle wheel to support the sliding gate. That is, the H-shaped cross-section sliding sleeve had no direct relationship with the overall rigidity of the telescopic sliding gate and the cooperation among the main moving parts constituting the gate. It can be seen that the H-shaped cross-section sliding sleeve in Comparative Document 2 and the H-shaped bushing in the invention had a substantive difference in the roles they played in their respective inventions. A person of ordinary skill in the art could not, starting from Comparative Document 1 and combining it with Comparative Document 2, obtain useful technical teaching about the invention; it would have required creative mental efforts to obtain it. Therefore, compared with the prior art, the technical solution of the invention was non-obvious to a person of ordinary skill in the art.

Second, the purpose and effect of the "Inertia Clamp Type Door" invention further demonstrate that it possesses prominent substantive features over the prior art. The court of first instance correctly held that, in determining whether an invention has prominent substantive features, consideration must be given not only to the degree of innovation of the technical solution itself, but also to the purpose and actual technical effect of the invention, taking the whole as an integrated whole. The purpose of the "Inertia Clamp Type Door" invention was to propose an inertia clamp type door whose connecting apparatus between the diagonal bars and the vertical straight bars is not only simple in structure, but also improves the rigidity of the door, making opening and closing movements light and quiet. To achieve this purpose, the technical solution of the invention adopted an H-section bushing fitted at the connection of each hinge pin of the door with the vertical straight bar. The use of the H-section bushing was intended to facilitate the sliding or rotation of the hinge pin on the edge of the notch of the vertical straight bar, and also to effectively fill the mechanical gaps between the main moving parts that constitute the entire door. The connection method was as follows: an H-section bushing was fitted at the end of each hinge pin connecting each diagonal bar of the door with each second vertical straight bar, and the edge of the vertical straight bar was installed in the groove of the H-section bushing. The function of the H-section bushing in the invention was not merely sliding or rotation, but also achieving the technical effects of convenient manufacturing and assembly, improving the overall rigidity of the door, and making the door opening and closing movement smooth, light, and quiet, thereby fulfilling the purpose of the entire invention. In contrast, the purpose of the invention in Comparative Document 1 was to solve the problem that a rolling gate with folding panels requires a large number of different components and manual riveting for assembly. Although its technical solution covered all the technical features in the preamble of the independent claim of the "Inertia Clamp Type Door" invention, because it lacked the distinguishing technical features of that invention, it obviously also lacked the technical effects of that invention. Comparative Document 2 describes a wheel device for the middle position of a courtyard fence gate. Although this wheel device also uses an H-section sliding sleeve, its purpose is to facilitate the sliding of the hinge pin on the two C-shaped rods of the additional device (the middle wheel frame) of the gate, and to cooperate with a locking device on the C-shaped rods, so that the middle wheel can support the rolling gate, thereby achieving the purpose of solving the problem of uneven ground in front of the courtyard, which causes the middle wheel to bear the heavy load of the fence, making opening and closing of the fence gate convenient and extending the service life of the wheel. It can be seen that the inventive purpose of the "Inertia Clamp Type Door" invention patent is completely different from that of the prior art. Because the purposes are different, the technical solutions adopted have substantial differences, and the technical effects achieved are also different. This technical effect was unexpected to a person of ordinary skill in the art. Therefore, when combining the technical solution, the purpose, and the technical effect of the "Inertia Clamp Type Door" invention as a whole and comparing them with the prior art, its prominent substantive features are obvious.

Third, compared with the prior art, the "Inertia Clamp Type Door" invention overcomes the shortcomings and deficiencies existing in the prior art and has made significant progress. On this point, neither the Patent Reexamination Board nor Hong Kong Mei Yi Metal Products Factory raised any objection.

In summary, the Patent Reexamination Board, based on Comparative Documents 1 and 2, concluded that the "Inertia Clamp Type Door" invention patent no longer possessed inventiveness, and issued a decision declaring the patent right for Invention No. 85101517, titled "Inertia Clamp Type Door," invalid. This decision lacked sufficient evidence. The judgment of the court of first instance, which set aside the Patent Reexamination Board's Decision No. 112 on the Examination of the Invalidation Declaration, was correct. However, in the judgment of the court of first instance, certain language and wording used in describing the facts and making the inventiveness determination were inappropriate. For example, the judgment compared individual technical contents from the specification of the invention (rather than the claim) with the prior art; the description of the purpose of the invention in Comparative Document 2 was inaccurate; the judgment also treated irrelevant matters, such as the "connection method of the H-shaped bushing and the diagonal bar" in the invention and Comparative Document 2, as distinctions between the invention and the prior art. These were improper and should be corrected. Nevertheless, these issues do not affect the correctness of the conclusion of the judgment of first instance. Looking at the entire case, the judgment of first instance had clear facts and applied the law correctly. In accordance with Item (1) of Article 61 of the Administrative Procedure Law, this Court rendered judgment on March 4, 1992: dismissing the appeal and affirming the judgment of first instance.
